correctness.rationale: All primitive two-cycle coordinates are integers. The two floor equalities yield explicit necessary-and-sufficient half-open intervals for each gap k. Integer-translation conjugacy reduces the phase to an interval of length q=1-lambda. Separating even and odd gaps produces two disjoint nested interval towers, from which the exact N>=m probabilities follow. A direct integer-count argument gives the uniform triangular phase approximation with error at most epsilon, and a Lipschitz comparison of positive parts yields the Kolmogorov error bound 6epsilon/(2-epsilon). Bounded scaled support gives moment limits. The standalone standard-library verifier passed 3,208 independent exact-rational assertions, including endpoints; no infinite statement depends on those finite samples. At each phase the primitive gaps form a consecutive parity class; coupling its uniformly selected gap index to a unit uniform random variable with error at most two integer steps, combined with the triangular phase bound and vanishing empty-phase probability, proves joint convergence to (T,2TV). The product of two independent unit uniforms has density -log(g) and moments 1/(r+1)^2. An additional 16 exact-rational near-critical first- and second-moment comparisons passed.

value.rationale: The source identifies an infinite-cycle singular slope but only gives individual fixed-parameter counts. The canonical integer-translation conjugacy quotient creates a natural finite parameter-phase space on which cycle multiplicity has an exact distribution. The two nested tower structure implies nearly uniform finite critical multiplicities, a sharp pointwise tent-profile limit, and the same nondegenerate phase-law from a contracting and an expanding side. This quantifies how the infinite family of two-cycles emerges and is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a rehash of a known single-parameter table. The two-stage selected-cycle gap has the nonuniform limiting density -log(g), giving additional geometric information beyond multiplicity and sharply separating phase-uniform sampling from global cycle-uniform sampling.
